section.title: §3.4 Public artifacts and CORS
section.summary: A visitor's browser fetches and runs the partner network. The visitor's page is the origin of calls the network makes from that browser.

answerSentences.partner-call: The partner network runs in the visitor's browser, making the call from the visitor's page across origins.
answerSentences.caller-origin: Use the origin of the visitor's page, where the browser runs the partner network.
answerSentences.preflight: The browser makes the cross-origin request from the page running the partner network.

section.title: Transports
section.summary: An MCP server using HTTP is reached through one endpoint. The server should check the Origin header on incoming requests.

answerSentences.partner-call: Serve HTTP MCP at a single endpoint and validate the request's Origin header.
answerSentences.caller-origin: The MCP server should also validate the Origin header it receives.
answerSentences.preflight: One HTTP endpoint serves MCP, and the server should validate the Origin header.

section.title: CORS
section.summary: To let a page on another origin call the endpoint, the server needs an Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header that covers that page's origin. The server also needs to handle the browser's preflight request.

answerSentences.partner-call: Return Access-Control-Allow-Origin for the caller's origin and respond to the browser's preflight request.
answerSentences.caller-origin: The endpoint's Access-Control-Allow-Origin response needs to cover that page's origin.
answerSentences.preflight: When the browser sends a preflight, the endpoint needs to answer it before the cross-origin call can proceed.

questions.prompt: A partner network runs in my visitor's browser. What does my MCP endpoint need so that the partner can call it?
Which origin should my server allow when a partner network runs in a visitor's browser?
How does a browser preflight fit into a call to my MCP endpoint?
